newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds of London raises minimum deposits for Names.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds of London raises minimum deposits for Names.

text.p: Lloyds of London on Thursday put forward proposals which will increase the minimum amounts Names must provide to support their underwriting activities.

Following a report from a working party set up to look at the insurance market's structure, Names -- the traditional backers of Lloyds -- will be required to provide at least 32.5 percent of amounts they underwrite next year and 37.5 percent in the following year and thereafter.

At present Names must put up between 20 and 30 percent of their underwriting capacity as deposits at Lloyds, compared with 50 percent for corporate investors. Lloyds said it would also introduce a requirement for Names to show evidence of assets totalling 50 percent of premiums underwritten by them.

Lloyds also intends ending the differential system of holding deposits at Lloyds associated with different categories of membership. It will require members to reconfirm the wealth backing their underwriting and the minimum of total means will be increased to reach 350,000 pounds ($568,000) by 1999, from its present level of 250,000 pounds.

Lloyds is still smarting from massive claims suffered by the market between 1988 and 1992. The changes were prompted by losses totalling eight billion pounds during that period, which at one stage threatened to sink the centuries old market.

They also led to the introduction of corporate capital for the first time and a fall in the number of Names to below 10,000 for the first time, from over 34,000 in 1989. Corporate funds now account for around 44 percent of this year's 10.3 billion pound capacity.
